topic: Binomial Theorem for Positive Integral Index
title: Binomial Theorem in One Line Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Multiplying (a + b) by itself ten times fills a whole page. The binomial theorem does it in one line. In this animated lesson on NCERT Chapter 7, Binomial Theorem, three friends ordering tea or coffee show where every term and every number in the expansion comes from.

You will watch all eight orders for (a + b)^3 get sorted live, see why each number in front is an nCr, let n count up from 1 to 10 as the numbers grow into a hill, and build the theorem in four small steps. Then a square picture shows why (a + b)^2 is not a^2 + b^2, a worked example expands (x + 2)^4, the exam trap fixes the signs in (x - 2)^4, and an original JEE Main pattern question uses the sum of coefficients. A recap card and three questions to check yourself close the lesson.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
